summary.intent: Finish and ship Wave 1 of a multi-workstream effort in the callisto repo: commit, push and open PRs for W10 and W9a, alongside the already-open W9b PR, after two of three workflow agents died.
summary.outcome: W10 was committed and opened as PR #223, with W9b already open as #222. The W9a status-versus-version resolver reproduction tests (8 passing agreement tests, 6 ignored divergences) passed `just ci` (exit 0), but the commit and PR had not yet been made.

repo: Gate is `just ci`; the repo also has a `check-api` step that flags public API changes, and changesets are used with a `minor` level and a 'Breaking:' list for breaking changes.
Work is organized in per-workstream worktrees (W9a, W9b, W10), entered and exited with EnterWorktree/ExitWorktree.
Divergences between expected and actual behavior are captured as `#[ignore]`d tests alongside passing agreement tests (crates/callisto-cli/tests/status_version_selector_tests.rs).
W10 gives every Cargo dependency declaration its own edge and rewrite. `DependencyEntry`, `DepEdge` and `RewriteKey` gain a `locator`, and `Manifest::update_dependency_spec` now takes one.
The Python ecosystem has the same defect as W10 (a requirement declared twice with different constraints); it is recorded but not fixed.
W9b makes a promoted pre-release key that disagrees with its package's baseline fail with E305 naming both keys and versions, rather than silently dropping a version.

code.finding: New W9a test file: 8 agreement tests pass and 6 `#[ignore]`d tests encode resolver divergences. Passed `just ci`.

workflow: When background agents die on a dropped connection, their worktrees may hold nearly complete work, so finishing and verifying it directly can beat rerunning the agents.
Independent PRs on `main` are preferable to a forced stack when the changes touch disjoint files.
Verify a new test genuinely fails without the fix (W10's black-box tests fail on `main`, W9b's fail with the check disabled) and get an independent review for behavior-changing PRs.
Read the gate's own exit line and tree state after a background `just ci` completes, instead of trusting the notification alone.

friction: Two of three workflow agents died on a dropped connection after about 50 minutes, so the assistant had to finish and verify their work manually.
Commits and gates for the affected workstreams ended up authored by the assistant rather than the agents.
open_items: Open the W9a PR now that its gate has passed (the commit and PR were still pending).
Python sibling of the W10 defect (requirement declared twice with different constraints) is recorded, not fixed.
The six `#[ignore]`d W9a divergence tests still need resolution.
User decisions are pending on D01's historical owner join and wire policy, W3's hash and retry design, and Python dev groups.
User may want #222, #223 and the W9a PR chained as a stack instead of independent PRs.
